name: GGUF Q2_K / Q2_K_S (2-bit K-quant)
bits: 2.63 avg (Q2_K_S 2.9697 bpw, Q2_K 3.1593 bpw as measured by llama.cpp on Llama-3.1-8B)
quality_delta: Only the unified Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct study was found for the 2-bit K-quant tier. The closest measured point is Q3_K_S (3.9960 bpw, same family): WikiText-2 ppl 8.96 vs 7.32 FP16, GSM8K 68.31 vs 77.63, IFEval 71.87 vs 78.93, unweighted 5-benchmark mean 65.49 vs 69.47 (quant-gguf-kquant-study). No published perplexity for plain Q2_K/Q2_K_S was located, so none recorded.
notes: Q2_K is the most aggressive point in the K-quant family and the practical floor. Structurally a 256-value super-block split into 16 sub-blocks of 16, where the 2-bit codes carry an extra per-sub-block min that recovers some dynamic range - the 'K' in k-quant. This is a Q*_K type, NOT the legacy Q2_0, which the allowed scheme enum has no slot for. Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). Llama.cpp CPU decode on that study's dual Xeon 8488C: Q2_K_S 90.01 tok/s tg128 vs 29.17 for F16, but Q2_K 79.85 and prompt processing *drops* to 784.45 vs 923.49 tok/s (quant-llamacpp-quantize-readme). Below ~3 bits expect visible multi-step-reasoning loss.
